title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is an 89-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He has been on long-term insulin therapy and currently does not take any other medications for his glucose management. He reports stable feelings overall but notes persistent sensations in his feet. He also mentions experiencing mild polyneuropathy. He reports that these sensations are constant but do not interfere significantly with his mobility. He denies any recent episodes of severe symptoms.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term use)

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Neurological exam shows diminished sensation to light touch in the distal lower extremities. Reflexes are diminished at the ankles. Skin is intact without ulcerations.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current insulin regimen.
2. Polyneuropathy: The patient presents with peripheral neuropathy; however, the provider notes this is not related to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Monitor blood glucose levels at home. Follow up in three months for a repeat evaluation of his polyneuropathy and diabetes management.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: The provider states the polyneuropathy is not diabetic: code diabetes without complications and the polyneuropathy separately.
Polyneuropathy not due to diabetes is coded separately (G62.9 when no cause is specified).
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Documentation of another cause overrides the 'with' presumption.
The polyneuropathy still needs its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
